transcript.text: I reviewed the securities team's call notes and confirmed that the reporting group discussed seeking a board seat with the issuer's largest shareholder. This discussion occurred after the draft Schedule 13G was circulated, and I have not yet updated the filing classification or the purpose section of the draft. This is significant because a board seat discussion is inconsistent with a passive-investment position, which is the premise of the Schedule 13G classification in the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Thank you, Evan. That's very significant. Now let me share my reconciliation results. I reconciled the prime-broker confirmations and affiliate accounts and found that the reporting group beneficially owns exactly 6.4% of the issuer's outstanding shares, including cash-settled positions that must be included. My reconciliation spreadsheet was completed after the draft circulated and has not yet been attached to the filing package. This percentage needs to be incorporated into the filing, and combined with Evan's finding about the board seat discussion, it appears the Schedule 13G classification may need to be reconsidered.

decisions.purpose_statement: The reporting group acquired shares of the issuer and discussed seeking a board seat with the issuer's largest shareholder, indicating a non-passive investment purpose inconsistent with Schedule 13G eligibility.

commitments.detail: Update the filing classification from Schedule 13G to Schedule 13D and revise the purpose statement to reflect the board seat discussion and non-passive investment position.
Attach the completed reconciliation spreadsheet to the filing package and incorporate the 6.4% beneficial ownership figure, including cash-settled positions, into the Schedule 13D.
